text:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mostly by trolls and lamias.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Perhaps you have already come across creatures touched by the Astral. Under its influence they change, and more often than not they change for the worse...

The Astral Horn is just such a creature. It is a unicorn turned into a dangerous monster. Even reaching it will not be easy, let alone defeating it. But there is something I do know… Once you find the island of the Astral Horn, you will have to hack your way through the astral crystals. Quite literally. You need the Hammer of Pain. You can obtain the hammer itself by defeating Splasher, a dangerous water elemental. Then, fighting the granite trolls, you will collect Shards of Pain. The power hidden in them will let you charge your weapon with magic. That can be done in the June ruins guarded by a cyclops nicknamed Stomper. And only once you have that weapon will you be able to break through the magic shield barring the way to the Horn's lair. I do not know what awaits you there. Be ready for anything. All that is known is that the Horn is not easy to find: it knows how to hide.

Bosses: Splasher, Stomper, Astral Horn.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Gallery: None :/

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Pearl Ring and the Tropical Atoll.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by humanoid toads.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Hm-m... I have heard of such an islet in the depths of the Astral, yes, though I confess I have never set foot on it myself. Nasty tales are told about that place. Ships go missing there, or so they say... A pilot I know told me that near that island all the equipment starts playing up, the reactor boils over, and the visor goes completely mad! But that is not all. Once, in some port, I met a thoroughly drunk orc who, by his own account, had served as cook on an Imperial trading schooner. And he told me that their ship had been wrecked on that atoll. He spoke of wandering undead, of some savages who feed on people, of an ugly idol... To be honest, I did not pay much attention to his drunken babble. But you, well, if you decide to put in at that atoll, don't let go of your weapon!

Bosses: Hump, Scabies, Pimple, Dead Captain.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by undead.

Story:

We arrive on the island, and a family of Seekers asks us for help. Lara, Indie and Nathan need to get into the tower for artifacts; to do so, several shards have to be collected and the sentry blocking the passage defeated. First we head into the thicket, where its inhabitants greet us aggressively; once we have cleared the thicket we find Sylvan, who complains that he will have to drive us off the allod himself. We defeat him, and Indie takes the shard. Next we make our way through the swamp, killing everyone who crosses our path, and reach the Silent Guard, who will not let us go further. Once they are defeated, Lara finds one more shard. We make our way through the ruins, again killing enemies. We find a passage, but it is guarded by the Sentry; we activate it and defeat it. After that the way into the Tower opens, and together with the Seeker family we defeat Veliyar. The gibberlings thank us for our help.

Bosses: Sylvan, Kodo the Silent and Nigan the Silent, Sentry, Veliyar.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to …

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian cemetery full of undead.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Yes, I have seen that islet. It really is a graveyard, and it really is peaceful. An old Kanian cemetery, one more forgotten shard of a perished world. A quiet place, a sad one. Dark trees, mist over the marshes, leaning gravestones... And in the depths some shadows drift and little lights flicker. Grief and dread simply breathe from it. I flew past it once, but decided not to land. Trust my experience: don't disturb the dead, or they will disturb you so badly you'll remember it all your life!

Bosses: Ferryman, Zhiroslav Glumeevich, Hell Sheer, Volokh Kromeshnikov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Gipat.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by goblins.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I happened to go there as part of a missionary and educational mission. You see, a tribe of utterly wild goblins lives on the White Mountain. The poor wretches do not even know who the Great Nezeb is! A thoroughly benighted people, and an aggressive one too! They wanted to sacrifice our missionaries to some scaly creature which the local goblins consider — just imagine — a god! Sacrilege, pure and simple!

When the missionaries and I left the island, a punitive detachment of the Committee arrived there to instil in the filthy pagans the fundamentals of the true faith, mutual respect and reverence for the Trinity Church. What happened on the island I do not know, but I do know that the Committee men came back from the island thoroughly battered and as furious as a thousand dragons, after which the coordinates of the island and the records of the two expeditions the Empire had made to the White Mountain were classified. But from rumours and gossip I heard of some idol worshipped by the shaggy wild runts, which supposedly gave its servants the strength to cope with seasoned Imperial fighters. If your path leads to the White Mountain, remember: fanatics do not heed the voice of reason. Brute force is the only thing they understand well!

Bosses: Mosol, Potbelly, Kazhetan, I'do-ol.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a secret laboratory.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Yes, I have heard of such a town. White 17 is a classified military settlement hidden somewhere deep in the Astral. And, as far as I know, there is something there to hide. You see, in White 17 Imperial scientists were engaged in extremely dangerous research. I don't know for sure, but rumour has it that Nomarkh Ebol, the lead researcher, maintained a very close relationship with Yasskul Setnakhte. Well, I have already told you about Yasskul Setnakhte and the incident at Lab Nine. And recently contact with White 17 was lost. Completely. Not a letter, not a messenger, not a single word... I fear some misfortune may have struck there, like the one that befell General Plague and his subordinates. So if in your wanderings you come across a snow-covered island guarded by Imperial soldiers, better turn back at once. But if you do risk landing there and get into trouble, look for Valentin Shtammin, an acquaintance of mine. He is listed there as chief mechanic, I believe. Oh, my heart tells me something is wrong with this White 17...

Bosses: Distemper, Venomisk, Crunch, Nomarkh Ebol.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by smugglers and the like.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Thanks be to Yasker, the Empire has no shortage of places for cultured recreation. If you like, go to the cinema; if you like, to a museum or a library; if you like, take a trip to a sanatorium, or to the Summer Atoll. Not enough excitement in your life — then play the sports lottery! And yet even here we still have elements for whom such entertainments are not enough; they want something hotter and more forbidden. And this in the Empire — as for the debauchery that goes on abroad, I simply keep silent! Well, as long as there is demand, there will be supply. In short, one crafty goblin found a stable islet in the Astral and set up an arena for gladiatorial fights there. Almost like on Yazes — only without demons, but with gambling and young ladies of dubious reputation. What riff-raff does not hang about there: mercenaries, and smugglers, and slave traders... They drink, place bets, cut each other for nothing. Shame and disgrace! Decent people have no business there, mark my words.

Bosses: Mussle, Spartacus, Cerbarath, Caligula.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, formerly Kanian.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

In my wanderings I always give Wolf Isle a wide berth. An ancient legend tied to this deadly place tells of a Kanian village that became a feeding ground for a werewolf. They say that long, long ago a Kanian druid named Vseslav the Charming grew so close to the wolves living on the island that he learned to change into wolf shape. He became the leader of the pack, and his neighbours its first victims. In time nobody was left there but wolves and werewolves. Hapless travellers who dare to land on the island become a welcome treat for its inhabitants. If you long to perform a heroic deed, Wolf Isle is quite a fitting place. But here is my advice: think a hundred times before you challenge the pack!

Bosses: Chernobog, the Bane of Wolf Isle, Vseslav the Charming.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Based on the Umoir Shard.

Climate: Wasteland, part of the Architects' universe.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Architects.

Story:

And they never did manage to finish off the damned Architects. The main attack was broken with the greatest effort, but at one moment those creatures scattered all over the world. Then a captain I know told me: he saw a familiar island in the deep Astral, once so very green, a real oasis. Now it is stark naked. Only those blue spires stick out. And beasts live there. They stare with a dead gaze. Their big eyes glow blue. Ugh, it gives me goosebumps… The Architects must have settled there and are remaking everything again in their own wretched likeness. Oh, if only someone would smash them to pieces…

Bosses: Pteros, Oculus, Arctus, Zero.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a termite nest.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What do astronauts fear? Everyone knows: demons and anomalies. But recently another plague has appeared. One after another, battered ships came into port, and their crews told of swarms of termites flying through the Astral as if across a green lawn. Once such a swarm flew all the way to Nezebgrad itself! They were shot down, of course, while still on approach, but the question remained: how do these insects scurry about in a hostile medium that dissolves everything, living and non-living? I heard that a private merchant managed to catch a few specimens and dissect them. In the insects' abdomens he found traces of meteorite dust — that is what protected them! Now the Free Traders promise a tidy sum to anyone who finds the nest of these creatures. Many rushed off in search of it... Only, I fear, it is their own death they are searching for. Can you imagine how huge the termite mound must be? If I knew where it was — be there meteorite, gold or gems — I would give it a wide berth!

Bosses: Ground Beetle, Murava, Itch, Chrysalis.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by lamias and drakes.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ugh, what a question! Rotswamp is the vilest place in the Astral. It squelches underfoot, drips down your collar, insects swarm in the mud, and the fog is so thick you can't see your own feet. In short, Rotswamp is the vilest swamp in the world! And how many travellers have vanished there... Wherever you go, you run straight into dangerous creatures! When I had the bad luck to end up in that stinking swamp with an expedition, on the very first day we lost three guards in fights with hydras. Horrible creatures that spit venom, and the oldest hydra, which we nicknamed Echidna, bit a pack horse in half in one go!

At night we were woken by terrible screams — lamias armed to the teeth attacked the camp, cut down the sentry and rushed at us, shouting something about two sisters thirsting for our blood. We barely fought them off! But in retreating we went into the very depths of the swamp, and that is where the main danger lay in wait for us. We had not even had time to wonder why the lamias had stopped pursuing us when a huge drake swooped from the night sky straight onto our party, pouring fire over everything around, while smaller drakes circled overhead, making sure none of us escaped. I survived only by a miracle — I fell into the mud, buried myself in it, and the drakes did not notice me. My comrades were not so lucky… By morning, having waited until the drakes finished their bloody feast and flew away, I crept back to the ship. Utterly exhausted, wounded and covered in mud from head to toe, at the sight of the ship waiting for us I almost wept with relief, and I swore that I would never again set foot in that cursed place!

Bosses: Echidna, Euriala and Stheno, Old Swamper, Venomwing.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Tep's cultists.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, so the rumours about that island have reached you too? A mysterious place. An ancient June forge, now seized by Tep's cultists. What goes on there, nobody knows. I heard of a group of desperate travellers who dared to penetrate the belly of the ancient volcano where the forge is located. Only one managed to come back. According to him, Tep's cultists are trying to take control of the ancient June mechanisms, to make them their loyal servants. If they succeed… The genius of the June plus the madness of Tep... Oh dear, oh dear... Be extremely careful if you dare to challenge this explosive mixture.

Bosses: Tep's Punisher, Tep's Rider, Dark Mistress, Shadow Devourer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

Climate: Desert, closest to the Den.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Tep's cultists.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

During one of my expeditions I was... hm... unlucky enough to visit the Tomb Isle. On my first visit it was a deserted place keeping the peace of one of Tep's Pyramids. My second visit was a vivid confirmation of the sad fact that Tep's cult has been restored. Now his followers rule the Tomb. They use stone elementals to dig out the Pyramid. I do not know what they are looking for there — my companions and I, many of whom were seriously wounded in the fight, had to leave the island in a hurry. I am sure nothing good can be expected from the activities of Tep's followers. I ask you to find that island and put an end to the cultists' doings. You will have to fight both them and their stone elementals. And most importantly — destroy Isdes, Tep's high priest, who leads the excavation of the Pyramid.

Bosses: Variant 1: Tep's Prelate, Tailstabber, Isdes. Variant 2: Longbelly, Tep's Prelate, Isdes, Sefnut.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Pearl Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Draconids.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know little about the jungles of Mboa-Mboa. Once we went far, far away, into the very deepest layers of the Astral. We were already thinking of turning back when land appeared on the horizon. We came closer and gasped — what beauty! Everything green, blooming, fragrant, butterflies of every colour of the rainbow flying about, monkeys jumping from palm to palm... Not an island — paradise! Well, that is what we thought until we went ashore. And there... mercy me! I had not seen such hungry creatures in a long time! Huge snakes, bloodsucking mosquitoes, crocodiles with jaws like a trap. So we ran back to the ship, and ran straight into the local aborigines — and next to them the crocodiles seemed a trifle. The scoundrels almost cut us to ribbons. Little, but vicious! After that it only got worse — we escaped the forest folk and ran into Draconids. They gladly invited us to dinner, with us in the role of first course, second course and dessert, so we ran back twice as fast! In short, I will never set foot in those jungles again. To the demons with such cruises!

Bosses: Swiss, Zuul, Boomer, Tom-Tom.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

Gallery: no information.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Kanian allod, though vampires of the House de Doucer have settled there alongside the Kanians.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Who would have thought that people and vampires could live in peace anywhere? But, believe it or not, there is such a place! It is called Enoch Isle. Once Enoch was a backwater islet of two villages. And not so long ago vampires who had renounced their creator, Armando de Doucer, arrived on the island. Somehow they came to an agreement with the peasants and receive blood in exchange for their goods, healing magic and other useful things. You won't believe it, but I saw with my own eyes that people and vampires live there in perfect harmony! But everything changed when werewolves appeared on Enoch. A cruel pack of half-sentient beasts invaded Enoch, and peaceful life came to an end. Their leader, the former bandit chieftain Lyut the Bobtailed, swore to devour everyone who does not bow before him. The vampires shut themselves off from the werewolves with magical barriers, closing the passages between the villages, and together with the peasants they hold back the monsters' attacks with their last strength. So if your adventures take you to Enoch, get ready for a fierce battle! Until you manage to clear both villages of werewolves completely, you will not get to their leader.

Bosses: Murk, Paul de Doucer, Vasilissa the Terrible, Lyut the Bobtailed.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Confrontation island.

Addendum: Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

Climate: Temperate and tundra; the allod consists of four shards.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by elemental spirits and the June.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Forgotten Temple? And what, may I ask, interested you in that cursed place? Believe me, anyone who gets there will want to forget the nightmares they lived through as soon as possible. Once it was a heap of June ruins of no interest to anyone, in the middle of an islet that not even the demons cared about, but then the Wormfaces reached the temple and awakened the flame that had slumbered in the temple for centuries. The island blazed like a torch until, by a whim of fate, it collided with an icy fragment of another island. Now half of the island on which the temple stands breathes heat, while on the other half you can freeze to the bone. Besides, it is full of aggressive elementals, old but still working guardian golems, and Wormfaces who very much dislike strangers. Still, among the Historians there are madmen ready to risk their lives for knowledge. I heard that not long ago the expedition of Martin de Blizare set off for the Forgotten Temple... And nobody has heard of that expedition since!

Bosses: Glacier, Ekaterina Arhivina, Sleepless Guard, Az and Yaz.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the grave of a June hunter.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever heard of the island of Vortex? A lump of ice-covered land floating in the Astral. The grave of a Great Dragon that died back in the time of the June. For many thousands of years its ghost has guarded its grave. Meanwhile the depths of this island hold considerable reserves of meteorite iron. The Empire has a vital interest in capturing it. Perhaps you will manage to do it? Then remember this. To reach the ghost you will have to fight ice elementals, wild yetis living in a cave, and harpies guarding the passage to the Great Dragon's grave. Only once you are next to it will you be able to see the ghost and defeat it. Will you take it on?

Bosses: Yeti Tribal Chief, Vladimir Evdokimov, Ghost of the Great Dragon.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Confrontation island.

Addendum: Based on the Grave Island. Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I have been on that island. Bliss: green forests, singing streams... There stands a posad — bigger than a village, smaller than a town. Red walls, a church with a bell tower, prosperous and friendly people. In a word, it is pleasant to visit and profitable to trade there. True, they say some bandits have recently started threatening them. Well, they are not poor folk — they have enough gold to hire mercenaries. Or perhaps you will help them, show some heroism? We clear the allod, kill the bandits, and at the end the warlock too.

Story allod:

Catherina sent the Heroes to this island to obtain a real Firebird. The heroes set off. But an adventure awaited them as if they had truly stepped into a fairy tale. For first they clashed with dashing bandits who were robbing the villagers. They dealt with them and rescued the headman, who told them that the local druid, Nikodim Farouche, had the bird. And for his rescue the headman gave them a horse which could be traded for the bird. But on the way a werewolf attacked the heroes and devoured the horse; defeated, however, it promised to enter their service. Nikodim, of course, refused to simply hand over the bird and demanded another such horse, one that belonged to the local sorcerer — Mira Hooves. So the heroes went to Mira Hooves. For the horse he demanded that they perform three services for him. At first he asked them to do all sorts of nonsense, and then he gave them a hard task — the warlock Newsor Rotheart, he said, had abducted a maiden whom Mira Hooves wanted to take as his bride.

The heroes had to go and fight the warlock. Though he commanded the dead, he was nevertheless defeated and fled in disgrace. They returned to Mira Hooves with the rescued maiden, Milava Clairante. But he had already forgotten the bargain — so they had to calm him down too. Taking the horse, they went to Nikodim, but he too wanted Milava for himself. So he also had to be given a punch on the nose. And when they finally came to the pier with the bird, the two Gubarevsky brothers were waiting there, wanting to take the Firebird for themselves and bring it to Catherina themselves. They had to be dealt with as well.

Bosses:

Astral island: Forest Bear, Penny Pincher, Mira Hooves, Newsor Rotheart.

Story island: Newsor Rotheart, Nikodim Farouche, the Gubarevsky brothers.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Draconids.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Oh, I would not advise you to get mixed up with the Draconids. Dangerous creatures. Even the Demon Hunters, who have made an alliance with them, do not fully trust these beings. And why is that? Because the Draconids guard their secrets like the apple of their eye! And do not trust them even to their friends. I do not know what secret is kept in the Green Maze. The Historians who tried to explore it never managed to get into its far part, access to which is closed by a magic barrier. As soon as they tried to get past it, two supreme Draconids appeared, two Guardians of the Limit, as they call themselves, and drove the Historians out. Since then the Draconids meet all uninvited guests with steel. If you have a taste for risk, you may try to uncover the secret of the Green Maze. But you will have to find your way through the ancient ruins on your own.

Bosses: Version 1: Supreme Spellcaster, Supreme Healer, Cursed Warrior. Version 2: Supreme Spellcaster, Supreme Healer, Reborn Warrior, Twice Born.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Frontier.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by aviaks and harpies.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Oh, that is a very interesting place. And a dangerous one! The Land of a Thousand Wings is a jumble of cliffs and the fragments of ancient buildings destroyed centuries ago. Three islands are linked by narrow little bridges that offer a dizzying view. And the Land of a Thousand Wings is inhabited by the only ones who can exist there without the constant risk of falling into the Astral or breaking their necks on the mountain slopes. I am talking about aviaks and harpies. As far as I understood, the aviaks came to the Land of a Thousand Wings first, while the harpies invaded the island much later, and it all ended in a big fight. But somehow Cual the Stormbearer, the aviak elder, managed to tame the unruly harpies. He and the queen of the harpies made peace, and now these two peoples live in complete harmony, helping each other in every way. I even suspect that between Cual himself and Olivia the Temptress there is something more than a business relationship. But that is beside the point. When I was a guest on that island, I was always amazed by Cual's wisdom and lively mind. He even managed to tame a wild manticore that lived in the ruins of an old temple! But in recent years the aviaks have shut themselves off from the rest of the world, accused both the League and the Empire of greed and stupidity, and deal harshly with anyone who dares to set foot on their land. I do not know what caused such sudden hatred of other peoples. Perhaps you will manage to find out the reason? But if you really are going to the Land of a Thousand Wings — get ready for a fierce battle!

Bosses: Olivia the Temptress, Silverwing, Murka, Cual the Stormbearer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to …

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a laboratory.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

And why are you suddenly interested in Zone 51? You are not even supposed to know the name "Zone 51". It is classified information, I'll have you know! But I think that you, as a direct participant in the events at Laboratory 13, have the right to hear the truth about this secret military base of the Empire in the distant Astral. Listen carefully, and mind you don't let it slip! Zone 51 is a military laboratory in which, after the incident at Laboratory 13, experiments continued on the study of psychic influence on the mass consciousness. Nomarkh Sadaffee, the head of the project, decided to combine psionic influence with physical modification of the body. In his opinion, the imperfect human organism is not able to fully manipulate even its own consciousness, let alone influence others. And so he decided to combine the prosthetic technologies of the Arisen with psionic abilities. The combat mechanisms that resulted, controlled by the power of thought, could have become the ideal army — tireless, needing no resources, incapable of betrayal... But it was Nomarkh Sadaffee himself who became the traitor! According to the latest information, he managed to destroy or subjugate the entire guard of Zone 51. Contact with the military base was lost, and now nobody knows what is going on there. So if you see a pretty tropical islet in the Astral, where gloomy metal hangars peer out among the green jungle, know this — landing on that island may be the biggest mistake of your life... And quite possibly the last!

Bosses: Scar, Kiddo, Crash, Nomarkh Sadaffee.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Jungles of Mboa-Mboa.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by aviaks.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A real pearl of the Astral! An Imperial resort would look perfect in such a place. But, alas, we will have to give up those plans — hostile aborigines now live on the island. Originally only one tribe of aviaks lived in the lagoon. At one time we managed to develop minimal trade relations with them. Pure barter — their hides and precious stones in exchange for our weapons. Unheard-of generosity on our part, by the way! Everyone knows there are no weapons in the world better than ours. But a little later certain pirates, whose names we will never learn now, attacked the lagoon, hoping to easily steal all our goods. The aviaks repelled the attack and in revenge plundered the pirates' ship. There, apparently, they found unhatched eggs and took them under their care. Unfortunately, they were lizard eggs. As soon as they hatched, the whole brood ran away from the aviaks to the other end of the island. Soon a second tribe of aborigines appeared in the lagoon. And so one stunt by idiots who had got their hands on the Astral dealt the Empire a blow, a weak one, but a blow nonetheless. The aviaks of Tusky Lagoon now regard the "wingless" with utter contempt. If you fly past, expect no hospitality.

Bosses: Rattle, Ssera-Hay, Cau the Stormbringer, Tsol the Bloodstained Feather.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian estate.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

There is nothing remarkable about that island. I don't really know much about it. It seems to be a Kanian allod. It is ruled by the illusionist mage Dobrinya Velikov. He calls himself "the Great", though I doubt his strength would really be enough to hold the island. A disagreeable person, I must say... He puffs himself up as if he really were Great, but in fact he is an ordinary fairground conjurer! There is a story that long, long ago a young sorceress, Alla by name, somehow got to that island without any ship at all. A magic whirlwind picked up her house, apparently, and threw it straight there. Along with her little dog and her nail file... There, on the island, Alla met strange but friendly creatures: a talking lion, an ancient lumberjack golem and a living scarecrow. Together with her new friends, having gone through incredible adventures, Alla finally reached the local mage, and he sent the hapless enchantress home. Although personally I suspect that the cause of that journey was not a whirlwind but a bottle of fortified liqueur and the great impressionability of that scatterbrained person, as well as the appetite for sensations of certain chatty scribblers!

Bosses: Brainless Scarecrow, Steel Lumberjack, Cowardly Lion, Dobrinya Velikov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian estate.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Oh, Boyar Jeer is a living legend! Though "living" — that depends on how you look at it... He is a necromancer, one of the best in the world. They even say he is a Great Mage! Whether they tell the truth or lie, I do not know: for many years he has lived alone on his estate, talking only to the dead. His peasants are another matter: merry, talkative, and not poor either — if the goods are good, they always have money. True, a merchant I know was there recently and told a strange thing. He comes off his ship, he says, lays out his goods, and the peasants don't even look his way: they all stand stock-still, staring at one point. He looked closer and saw that a ghostly mist seemed to spread over all of them... He took to his heels from there! Whether it's true or not, I do not know — I sell it as I bought it! If you are there — maybe you will find out the truth?

Story allod:

Catherina sent the heroes to Jeer to learn the skill of speaking with the dead. The problem was that Jeer took no apprentices. So a special approach had to be found. The heroes went to him and left empty-handed — Jeer defeated them and threw them into his dungeon. Only with the help of the Bogatyr whom Catherina had sent with them did they manage to break their chains and leave the prison. And on the way they freed another sorceress — Vasilissa Artful, who also thirsted for forbidden knowledge. The freed Vasilissa had a plan for making Jeer take apprentices after all. For that his death had to be found, and Jeer had hidden his death in a needle. He put the needle in a drake, the drake in a hare, and the hare in a chest, which he hung on a black oak. It was not easy to find Jeer's death, but they did manage to obtain it. And the old man had no choice but to agree to teach the heroes the language of the dead. And the needle in which his death was sealed stayed with Vasilissa.

Bosses: Clockwork Madman, Ill-Rot, Raven Tome, Vasilissa Artful.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by forest creatures and nature spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A strange little place... Either that island really exists, or it is a mirage, a phantom, a delusion. That island is covered with dense forests and deep swamps. All sorts of creatures live there, some sentient and some not so much. I saw kikimoras, satyrs, I even saw a talking fox! And most importantly — there are ghosts there without number! Mostly Kanians, seemingly alive and yet not. And they all obey the mistress of that place, Ziva is her name, I think — whether a human, or a bird, or some kind of spirit altogether. A peaceful little place; the mistress was welcoming to us that time, gave us rest and shelter. Only I heard from other travellers that some misfortune happened there recently — whether an unhappy love or some curse... In short, I would think twice about putting in at Iriy without holy water and loaded cannons!

Bosses: Bosk, Mister and Missus, Naiad, Marena.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Xadaganians.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What tricky questions you ask. And do you know that for that sort of thing you can end up in the Committee's dungeons? You see, even after the Cataclysm not all Xadaganians accepted Nezeb's rule. When the industrial revolution began in the Empire, some isolated allods inhabited by Xadaganians did not accept the new doctrine and went on living by the old customs. Dersaadet is just such a place. A shard, so to speak, of the old Empire, frozen in timelessness. There they do not believe in the Light, do not honour the saints of the Trinity Church, but pray to the Almighty in a mosque. Dersaadet is ruled by Sultan Mustapha al Muhad, and his power is boundless. And whoever wants to challenge it will have to deal with loyal janissaries and the magic of a cunning vizier. But if you come to Dersaadet in peace, generous hospitality awaits you, fine wines and delicacies such as the world has never seen!

Bosses: Minotaur, Mehmet Pasha, Rajima, Lamia Princess.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, cursed land.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by merchants and a circus troupe.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, I know that place. A rather gloomy little place, I must say. Once there was a circus there, a perfectly ordinary circus, with clowns, acrobats and a trained bear with a balalaika. But the place was not popular. Who would fly through the danger-filled Astral just to look at some jesters? And so the circus fell into complete neglect. And then three men turned up there, calling themselves professors, specialists in dreams and fantasies. They patched up the old circus buildings and sent invitations to their Carnival to anyone who wished to come. The masters of the Carnival guarantee the fulfilment of the most cherished desires, the rosiest dreams and the most incredible fantasies. As far as I'm concerned, they are all charlatans, every last one. They don't take money from anyone, by the way, which is very strange. Now if they wanted to line their pockets, then the point of such promises would at least be understandable. For now all I can advise you is — keep your ears pricked!

Bosses: Dread, Heat, Red Beard, Harlequin.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by lizards.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Surely you're not planning to join the Historians? Any Historian would give his right hand without a second thought to explore Koch-Itzmahl. Just imagine — a fully preserved temple from the heyday of the June empire. Not those pitiful ruins scattered everywhere, but a complete temple complex. I confess I only glimpsed it, and even then I nearly fell overboard in surprise! Bas-reliefs, frescoes, statues, carved columns... Ah, and how many secrets it hides, how many treasures... But there is no way to get to them! Lizards have overrun the whole island. When we tried to put ashore, they pelted us with spears, burned a huge hole in the sail with a fireball, and kept promising to tear out our hearts and lay them on the altar of their ancestors. Their chief, Shisskh, raged most of all. Ooh, vicious creatures! We had to turn round urgently and move on empty-handed. Clearing the temple of the lizards' presence is a good deed and pleasing to the Light... and a profitable one besides!

Bosses: Caiman, Lion, Bloodberry, Shisskh the Seven-Fingered.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Confrontation island.

Addendum: Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a large trading city.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Don't you know? "Where to, where to... To East Overshoe!" — that is how traders used to answer anyone too curious before casting off from the pier. And not without reason — on East Overshoe there was a rich trading city whose inhabitants talked in practically nothing but proverbs. Whatever you ask an Overshoer, he answers you with a saying. It was a rich city, and misfortune passed it by. The Overshoers grew so used to a quiet life that they would say, "we'll start shutting the gates when a crayfish whistles on the mountain". Well, the crayfish waited and waited, and then it whistled. They got what they bargained for. And yet they had been told — let sleeping trouble lie! The other day I flew past East Overshoe — everything has fallen into desolation, not a sound, not a rustle. But who knows what is really going on there? From afar it's just an abandoned city, but, as the saying goes, still waters run deep and devils live in them!

Bosses: Sleeping Trouble, Clop, Byak and Zyrk, the Noon Witch, Raak.

Type: Medium allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former gibberling settlement (captured by demons).

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Frost and cold — that is all I can say about Kyoltmark. I have not been there myself, but I know that one of the first gibberling ships was once wrecked on that icy rock. When League ships did eventually discover the rock a few years later, the surviving gibberlings had already settled on that miserable scrap of land, made themselves at home and flatly refused to leave the island that had become their home. But not so long ago misfortune struck — astral demons attacked the island. And what is strangest of all, they did not slaughter the inhabitants but took them captive. They say a mighty demon called the Thought Catcher turned all the gibberlings into his slaves, and now they serve him faithfully and devotedly. A terrible fate! If you find yourself on that island, you will not avoid a fight with the crazed gibberlings. Strike without pity — only empty shells are left of the locals, and the demons control their will!

Bosses: Fiend, Guur'Maan, Sharpclaw, Thought Catcher.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Island sizes:

Small allods — the smallest allods, mostly a single settlement.

Medium islands — larger islands, usually with several large settlements.

Large islands — have many settlements and various zones and regions.

Climate:

Desert — deserts, little vegetation, and palm trees.

Tropical — jungle and swampy jungle.

Temperate — the meadows and forests of the middle latitudes, coniferous and deciduous forest.

Taiga — mostly coniferous trees and snow cover.

Tundra — small trees or none at all, permafrost.

Wasteland — a blend of ordinary matter with the matter of another universe; also astral wasteland.

Affiliation:

League — population: Kanians, gibberlings and elves.

Imperial — population: Zem, Xadaganians and orcs.

Elven — population: elves only; not part of the League.

Neutral — population from both the League and the Empire, Free Traders and pirates. Also various lesser races (forest folk, lizards, etc.).
